title: Zephyrine and the Promise
premise: Ansel Joubert, widowed father running the last bookshop in the fading coastal town of Sainte-Rose, agrees to pose as the boyfriend of Zephyrine Delacroix at her family's vineyard reunion to shield her from her grandmother's matchmaking and her own decade-old broken engagement. What begins as a transactional arrangement deepens over one long weekend as Zephyrine reveals she has returned to sell the family estate — and Ansel realizes the reunion doubles as the deathbed gathering of the grandmother who once promised him something he has never claimed. When the will is read, Ansel must finally speak the rehearsed sentence — that he loved Zephyrine's mother, and through her, her all along — choosing inheritance of memory over the safe silence he has kept for ten years. The story ends with the estate saved not by money but by testimony, and the two of them opening the bookshop's shutters together on a Monday morning.
about_author: Kestrel Okonkwo is the pen name of a former archivist who spent years cataloguing the letters of families who never said what they meant. Writing from a small house above a shuttered cinema, Okonkwo crafts romances where love arrives late, on purpose, and costs exactly what it is worth.

chapters.title: The Terms of the Weekend
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Zephyrine walks into the bookshop with a proposition: be her date to the Delacroix reunion, and she'll pay off the shop's crushing debt. Ansel, desperate and skeptical, agrees after closing time — and recognizes her as the daughter of the woman he once loved. The emotional beat is wary transaction masking old grief, ending on the drive to the vineyard with a rehearsed backstory neither fully believes.

chapters.title: Dessert and the Long Table
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The reunion unfolds in staged intimacy that turns real: shared lies about how they met keep becoming true, and grandmother Odile studies Ansel with unsettling recognition. Zephyrine confesses she's selling the estate; Ansel learns Odile is dying and the will will be read Sunday. The beat is the fake date becoming too real by dessert — warmth arriving with dread attached.

chapters.title: What Odile Kept
chapters.summary: Zephyrine's POV. Zephyrine discovers a locked cedar chest of letters between her late mother and Ansel — a decade of unsent devotion — and realizes her fake boyfriend is the man her mother's letters mourned. Confronted, Ansel admits he promised Odile he'd stay away so Zephyrine could leave Sainte-Rose. The beat is betrayal curdling into understanding: every kindness of the weekend was also a long-delayed penance.

chapters.title: The Sentence, Spoken
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. At Sunday's will reading, Odile leaves the estate to whoever can answer one question: who kept the promise, and who broke it. Ansel stands and speaks the rehearsed sentence at last — claiming his love for Zephyrine's mother and for her — trading the inheritance of silence for testimony. Odile amends the will; the estate passes to both. The beat is release: grief spoken aloud becomes a shared future, and Monday opens with bookshop shutters and no more rehearsed lines.
